# SAMPL8 pKa reference version sensitivity

Published Research Note and reproducibility code. The fixed archival version is
[Zenodo 1.0.0](https://zenodo.org/records/23112909), published on 3 October 2026
as a Technical note, DOI [10.5281/zenodo.23112909](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23112909).
This repository provides the maintained reader guidance and the same frozen
scientific inputs, analysis, results, figures, tables, Research Note and SI.

## Read and download

| Purpose | Link |
| --- | --- |
| Formal publication and citation metadata | [Zenodo record](https://zenodo.org/records/23112909) |
| Research Note, fixed PDF | [Zenodo PDF](https://zenodo.org/records/23112909/files/N1_Session10_Research_Note.pdf?download=1) · [repository copy](manuscript/manuscript.pdf) · [Markdown](manuscript/manuscript.md) |
| Supplementary Information, fixed PDF | [Zenodo SI](https://zenodo.org/records/23112909/files/N1_Session10_Supplementary_Information.pdf?download=1) · [repository copy](manuscript/supplementary_information.pdf) · [Markdown](manuscript/supplementary_information.md) |
| Fixed reproducibility package | [Zenodo ZIP](https://zenodo.org/records/23112909/files/N1_Session10_Reproducibility_Package.zip?download=1) |
| Fixed delivery SHA-256 list | [Zenodo checksum file](https://zenodo.org/records/23112909/files/N1_RELEASE_SHA256.txt?download=1) |
| Maintained code and inputs | [analysis](analysis/N1_primary_analysis.py) · [frozen CSV](data/n1_frozen_inputs.csv) · [data provenance](data/README.md) |
| This post-release audit | [validation record](provenance/POST_RELEASE_VALIDATION.md) |

The PDFs and their Markdown sources preserve the fixed publication bytes. Their
references to a reserved DOI, a private repository, release review, or a possible
later ChemRxiv DOI describe preparation-time status. The Zenodo record and this
README provide the current publication status. No ChemRxiv submission or other
submission is planned as part of this dissemination endpoint.

## Scope and interpretation

N1 asks how fixed pKa prediction errors and relative calculation comparisons change
when original experimental references are replaced by post-challenge SiriusT3
values, keeping predictions and selected state transition (SST) assignments fixed.
The scope is exactly S8-2, S8-5, and S8-22 and four complete-case calculations:
COSMO-RS one pKa fit, EC-RISM, RFE-uESE-extra, and Chemaxon.

The subset MAE ordering changes: COSMO-RS one pKa fit and Chemaxon reverse order.
This is a deterministic result for a selected remeasurement subset. It does not
establish benchmark-wide ranking instability, experimental superiority, or general
method superiority. SST is a fixed framework; PST was not evaluated.

## Citation

For the Research Note and its accompanying archived compendium, cite:

Miyazaki, S. (2026). *Experimental reference version sensitivity of fixed SAMPL8
pKa predictions in a selected remeasurement subset* (Version 1.0.0). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23112909

This version-specific DOI identifies the Zenodo record containing the Research
Note, SI and reproducibility package. It is not a separate software-only DOI or a
ChemRxiv DOI. Use it to identify the fixed scientific publication.

`CITATION.cff` describes the repository software at its root and redirects the
preferred citation to the published Zenodo work using its full title. When citing
a particular maintained code revision, also state the repository URL and the
actual commit SHA used; the archival DOI alone does not identify later main
commits. The all-versions DOI, 10.5281/zenodo.23112908, is not the identifier of
this specific fixed version.

Author: Sho Miyazaki, Independent researcher, Tokyo, Japan.
Correspondence: shomiyazaki98@gmail.com. Funding, competing interests,
acknowledgments and AI assistance are disclosed in the Research Note; the exact
AI disclosure is also preserved in [AI_ASSISTANCE.md](manuscript/AI_ASSISTANCE.md).

## Reproduce the numerical analysis

Download and extract the Zenodo ZIP, or download this repository using **Code →
Download ZIP**, then open a terminal in the package root.
The supplied upstream files are sufficient; no external data download or
prediction calculation is needed. Input extraction and primary analysis use
only the Python standard library (tested with CPython 3.12.14).

For a Git checkout, export a separate working copy with `git archive` before
package verification. The unchanged verifier checks every package file and does
not ignore `.git` or virtual-environment directories. For example, from the
checkout run `git archive --format=zip --output=../n1-working-copy.zip HEAD`,
extract that ZIP elsewhere, and use its package root for the commands below.

Verify the shipped package before modifying any files:

```bash
python3 provenance/verify_package.py
python3 data/build_frozen_inputs.py
python3 analysis/N1_primary_analysis.py
python3 provenance/verify_package.py
```

The extraction verifies SHA-256 for four numerical source files and joins stable
source keys. The analysis verifies all 12 frozen cells, upstream original AEs,
both subset MAE orderings, and the COSMO-RS/Chemaxon arithmetic decomposition.
Outputs are `results/N1_primary_results.csv`, `results/N1_method_MAE.csv`, and
`results/validation.json`. They should match the shipped files byte for byte.
Scripts locate the package root from their own paths; the primary analysis also
accepts `--input` and `--output-dir` for comparison in another directory.

Calculations use Decimal precision 40. Display tables round cell values to two
decimals, main MAEs to three decimals and SI MAEs to six decimals; ordering uses
unrounded values. Experimental uncertainties are documented, not propagated.

On Windows, use `py -3` in place of `python3` if that is your Python launcher.
No shell-specific commands are required for this numerical workflow.

## Verify the figure, tables and PDF build

Run this optional build in a **separate disposable copy**. It overwrites generated
files in that copy; the shipped publication PDFs remain the canonical fixed files.
The pinned rendering dependencies are matplotlib 3.10.8 and ReportLab 4.4.9.
Use a virtual environment outside the package tree, or use the existing Python
environment, then run from the copied package root:

```bash
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python3 data/build_frozen_inputs.py
python3 analysis/N1_primary_analysis.py
python3 figures/make_figure_1.py
python3 provenance/build_manifest.py
python3 tables/make_tables.py
python3 manuscript/build_documents.py
```

Do not reorder the manifest/table/document steps: Table S4 consumes the source
manifest, and the documents consume generated tables. Compare regenerated outputs
with the shipped files before creating a new checksum list. Font files and
dependency versions can affect rendered bytes. The PDF builder uses installed
DejaVu fonts, `N1_FONT_DIR`, or matplotlib's bundled fonts. Numerical reproduction
and byte-identical rendering are distinct checks.

After an intentional rebuild of the disposable copy only:

```bash
python3 provenance/build_manifest.py --checksums
python3 provenance/verify_package.py
```

Regenerating checksums records the new local bytes; it does not demonstrate
agreement with the archived publication. Keep environments, caches and `.git`
outside a checksum-regeneration copy: the unchanged generator inventories all
package files except itself and Python bytecode/cache files.

## Fixed archive, maintained main and historical release

The Zenodo ZIP is the fixed publication archive. Main carries subsequent reader
guidance and citation corrections, with the scientific content frozen. The fixed
Research Note, SI, their source Markdown and all numerical/scientific files match
Zenodo. README, CITATION and post-release audit/checksum records intentionally
describe the maintained repository instead of duplicating the older archive.

[GitHub Release v1.0.0](https://github.com/shomiyazaki-ai/sampl8-pka-reference-sensitivity/releases/tag/v1.0.0)
points to initial commit `0c97cf7c46cd0a20c76f2337dc1bc6b048606a49`.
Its only assets are GitHub-generated source ZIP/tar.gz snapshots. They retain the
older preparation metadata and older manuscript/SI availability paragraphs; they
are **not identical to the Zenodo publication package**. Use the Zenodo links
above for the fixed publication and main for the maintained guidance. The old tag
and Release are retained as historical records, without moving or replacing them.

## Files, checksums and historical provenance

- `upstream/`: original source bytes and notices, with [attribution](upstream/ATTRIBUTION.md).
- `data/`, `analysis/`, `results/`: source extraction, frozen inputs and full-precision outputs.
- `figures/`, `tables/`, `manuscript/`: scientific assets, text sources and unchanged build scripts.
- `provenance/source_manifest.csv`: fixed, acyclic input/output identity set;
  its production dates and unreleased-at-production labels are historical.
- `provenance/SHA256SUMS.txt`: this maintained package's hashes, excluding itself.
  `verify_package.py` checks exact file coverage and source/table agreement.
- `provenance/SESSION10_METADATA_VALIDATION.json`: unchanged Session 10
  **pre-release** audit snapshot, not a post-release verification result.
- `provenance/FINAL_REBUILD_VALIDATION.json`, `provenance/history/`,
  `provenance/publication_status_check.md`: preserved earlier audit/status records.
  They do not assert the current publication state or the latest upstream paper version.
- `provenance/POST_RELEASE_VALIDATION.md`: this local post-release audit and its
  explicit pending remote deployment checks.

The Session 10 review bundle is a separate preparation-time evidence package,
not part of the published compendium; its historical checklists were not edited.
The approximately 63 MB original upstream snapshot ZIP is not bundled or needed
to run N1. Its comment commit and archive identity are preserved in
`provenance/snapshot.json`; the preserved source bytes identify the actual inputs.

## Licensing and attribution

N1 code is MIT. N1 manuscript, SI, figures, tables, documentation and derived data
are CC BY 4.0. Upstream files retain their original notices and attribution.
See [LICENSE](LICENSE), [LICENSE_CC-BY-4.0.txt](LICENSE_CC-BY-4.0.txt), and
[upstream/ATTRIBUTION.md](upstream/ATTRIBUTION.md). A GitHub license badge or the
software citation's MIT field does not relicense the whole mixed-content archive.
The Research Note discloses no specific external funding and no competing interests.
